rationale: Evaluating print/chart/video needs matched source media. No actual dataset or clip claims are supplied for a faithful visual comparison; medium icons would only repeat labels.
Lowered wing is interpreted figuratively as humility and mercy. A bird scene could literalize the image; the command/prohibition analysis already supplies the linguistic distinction.
Friend like mirror versus friend mirror already isolates the comparison particle. A mirror photograph cannot demonstrate its omission and would repeat the verbal example.
Students infer relations between two selected poetic ideas. No matched verses are supplied for a true causal or conditional connector, so an imposed flow would pre-answer analysis.
Character claims require quotations, actions and others testimony. No verified portrait or specific testimony is supplied; a desert/sea collage would stereotype the poet context.
Objective summary and evidence evaluation need the actual argument. No three source points are given to visualize without writing the student summary for them.
The slide already gives a full cause/behaviour/effect/solution example. Another chain duplicates it and a device photo cannot establish addiction or causality.
The old spring recording is analysed for audible pace and emotion. A water-source photograph would literalize a title without showing the tone students must hear.
Cinema here is an argument-weighing recording. A camera or filmstrip would be a genre label; no production process or source evidence is provided to visualize.
The ethics persuasive talk leaves evidence selection to students. An idealized youth scene would choose their example without helping the delivery rubric.
The unrealized-hope story requires personal characters and setting. A completed hopeful/disappointed scene would supply the original detail students are asked to create.
The hadith focuses on verbal restriction, metonymy and parallel clauses. Tongue/hand pictures would literalize the figure; the text already states the ethical application.
Martyrdom imagery is sensitive and the lesson needs verse-based emotion and context. No named subject or verified scene is supplied, and a generic memorial would not explain the poetic technique.
Added visibly literary schematic of highlighted stone within a dam; no engineering prediction or ending shown.
A third-class train interior would introduce unmentioned historical setting and costume. The analysis depends on specific events and dialogue revealing character, not carriage appearance.
Short/long sentences and concept development must be seen in an actual paragraph. No paragraph is supplied, and a brain picture would be a topic proxy.
Healthy/unhealthy contrast already names movement versus inactivity. Exercise imagery would repeat an example rather than reveal the textual antithesis or quality of evidence.
Latent abilities are the recording subject, but no concrete argument is transcribed. A talent icon would not teach evidence weighting and could preselect an interpretation.
The healthy-living talk has organization and delivery criteria. A meal or runner picture would select a lifestyle example without modelling reliable sourced persuasion.
The research report begins with the student own school/community question. A supplied chart would invent findings and bypass the requested hypothesis and sources.
The farewell sermon lesson analyses address, questions and repetition. An invented historical crowd scene would add identity and setting details without teaching those verbal effects.
Friend like mountain invites an omitted comparison quality. A literal mountain would privilege height over the stated stability and would not show explicit versus implicit wording.
The necklace story depends on a final reversal. A finished necklace image would add a design not in the summary and a plot picture would risk revealing the twist without improving the causal reading.
Palm and river description is evaluated through the child narrator. A stock date scene would choose sensory details and cannot show the change in the child understanding of the grandfather.
The elegance article is about evidence, opinion and alternatives, not clothes shopping. An outfit image could contradict the claim that elegance is behaviour and would not evaluate its reasons.
The white/black coins are a proverb, not literal colour. A money image would mislead; savings stages are already explicit with no amounts available for a valid budget chart.
The false-prayer recording needs audible pace and the listener inference. A prayer scene would infer religious details and cannot demonstrate deceptive tone.
The talk on inner worth requires chosen evidence. A face or jewel picture would impose appearance-based values rather than support organization and oral delivery.
Low motivation is the explanatory problem chosen for research. No measured causes are supplied, so a causal brain diagram or factor chart would invent evidence.
Added spatial official-letter structure, marked as teaching layout not a sent request.
The ancient advice requires wording and tribal context. A generic historical portrait would be invented and would not explain command versus prohibition or modern paraphrase.
Rashid Al Khidr biography asks students to link a real event to poetry. No dated milestones or verse pair are supplied for a responsible timeline or travel map.
Farewell feelings are inferred from description and dialogue. A stock farewell scene would fix age, relationship and setting not given by the source.
Existing added licensed wooden-dhow photograph directly clarifies ship shape and material for the qalaf craft term, without claiming to show every construction stage.
Pearl-diving recording analysis asks for tone, pacing and emotion. A diver photo could label the topic but would not supply the audible evidence the lesson targets.
The sea-resources talk leaves subject and reliable examples to students. A fish or shell collage would choose content without improving the speaking model.
The planning essay asks when and how with evidence. A supplied future timeline would impose a personal schedule while the text already explains writing organization.
Added open river versus frozen surface before literary interpretation, marked as schematic not a named place.
The river-ogress is an imaginary warning figure, and the social explanation is explicitly tentative. A monster picture would overstate its appearance and duplicate the fear cue.
The Finnish smith tale separates realistic craft from magic. No verified setting or tool details are supplied for a grounded scene; depicting the magic would preselect the imaginative interpretation.
Added licensed India locator with faithful visible two-shade source legend; no population values invented.
Myth/folktale/history are differentiated by function and evidence. A generic hero-monster image would illustrate only one pattern and falsely narrow the three-way comparison.
The phoenix is the listening subject but tone is the target. An ungrounded fire-bird picture could fix the legend before listening and would not show pace or pauses.
The myth summary talk asks students to choose a civilization and source. A ready-made myth image would choose the subject and episode for them.
The blind-prejudice essay needs documented evidence and solutions. A symbolic blindfold would literalize the phrase and could stereotype rather than explain the argument.
Whispering nature is personification and connotation. A face on a tree would literalize it; a forest photo cannot demonstrate the human action attributed by the words.
The enchanted-pool transformation is the consequence students analyse. An animal transformation illustration would reveal the magical event and add unsupported costume or setting.
The scale-and-gold tale already states a greed reversal. A gold/snake panel would repeat and spoil that reversal, not explain evidence about contrasting characters.
Gold properties, rarity, value and uses are already linked in words. A jewellery photo would narrow the uses, and a causal price diagram would overstate a simplified economic relation.
Sinbad uses a recurring departure/danger/escape/return pattern already supplied. An invented island adventure would imply a particular voyage absent from the text.
The storyteller recording is an evidence-weighing task. An audience illustration would label the role without showing the claims students must assess.
Students choose a heritage folktale for their presentation. A stock grandmother scene is not a model of evidence, source accuracy or delivery and would repeat the topic.
Unfair competition is an open explanatory problem across school/sport/trade. An illustrated cheating act would select a case before students research evidence and solutions.
Comparing short story and novel requires actual passages. Tree/branch shapes could imply structure without textual support, and an animal image would pre-answer the symbolic tradition.
The child viewpoint and poetic school dream require the exact narration. A schoolgirl scene would impose setting and appearance not established by the summary.
The old wall bears a specific fictional memory of coastal attack. A ruin photograph would falsely identify a place or historical event and cannot establish the narrator symbolism.
Character analysis needs thoughts, speech, actions and testimony from the sea story. No concrete episode is supplied for a faithful scene or filled evidence map.
The other-face story turns on revelation and viewpoint. A two-face image would be a literal title proxy and a filled reveal would pre-answer the student reading.
Nahma is experienced through sound and work rhythm; the lesson explicitly asks what audio adds. A music-note panel would only label genre and cannot show audible practice.
Majidi bin Dhaher recording analysis needs emotion and pacing. No verified portrait or audio segment supports a visual annotation; a poet icon would add no evidence.
The khurrafa talk asks students to select a folktale and deliver a source-based account. A generic magical scene would choose details instead of improve presentation criteria.
The shipbuilding speaking topic already has a separate factual/photo lesson in T2L05. Repeating its dhow photo here would label the subject rather than model oral delivery.
The homeland essay must build arguments from books and experience. A flag or house would pre-frame the emotional answer without adding the requested evidence or rebuttal.
Hunting is an explicitly two-sided argument task. A harmed-animal photograph would bias the decision and could distress students without helping them weigh claims.
The wolf title invites prediction from name and cover. A new wolf portrait could conflict with the original cover and would preselect a visual reading before the prediction.
Character mapping is assigned, but only Tawwaf is named. A filled network would invent secondary figures or relations; an empty central circle would repeat the instruction.
Students place a selected event on the plot and explain past/future links. No actual event sequence is supplied for a truthful curve or connectors.
Nature/others/self conflicts must be classified from specific moments. A wolf-versus-hunter scene would invent an episode and could suggest a definitive conflict not yet read.
Narration, description and dialogue are compared through a selected scene. No matched excerpt is supplied; a landscape could only label description rather than demonstrate technique.
The wolf is a symbolic distancing device, not a zoology target. A realistic wolf image would add appearance but not explain why an animal can reflect human values.
Identifying the climax and predicting what follows is the learning task. A filled plot curve would decide the very inference students are asked to support.
Two viewpoints must be compared about the same actual event. No matched statements are supplied; an eye icon or double portrait cannot show narrator effect.
The solution lesson revisits predictions and invites alternate endings. A fixed final scene would settle the ending and narrow the stated interpretations.
Character change needs a beginning trait, a changing event and end trait from the novel. The summary supplies the framework, not evidence for a filled diagram.
Adaptation requires the student to choose what narration becomes dialogue and what is omitted. A ready-made storyboard would take over that assessed selection.
The final project offers diary, justified ending, response or visual presentation. A completed wolf scene would bias the open creative choice rather than support the criteria.
